---
title: "Sonic Profile Exploration"
format: html
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)

# Create the dataset of Top 5 and comparison tracks
songs_data <- tibble(
  title = c(
    "SQUEEZE", "Oh Yeah?", "WALLFLOWER", "Give You the World", "Evergreen (Stripped)",
    "White Ferrari", "Japanese Denim", "Roommates", "Apocalypse",
    "good 4 u", "Blinding Lights", "Closer", "After Party"
  ),
  artist = c(
    "Dominic Fike", "Steve Lacy", "Dominic Fike", "Steve Lacy", "Omar Apollo",
    "Frank Ocean", "Daniel Caesar", "Malcolm Todd", "Cigarettes After Sex",
    "Olivia Rodrigo", "The Weeknd", "Ne-Yo", "Don Toliver"
  ),
  group = factor(
    c(
      rep("Top 5", 5),
      rep("Similar (Soul / Bedroom Pop)", 4),
      rep("Dissimilar (Uptempo / Dance / Trap)", 4)
    ),
    levels = c("Top 5", "Similar (Soul / Bedroom Pop)", "Dissimilar (Uptempo / Dance / Trap)")
  ),
  tempo = c(86, 92, 82, 78, 75, 60, 110, 88, 97, 167, 171, 126, 163),
  energy = c(52, 48, 44, 45, 30, 18, 42, 50, 47, 66, 73, 77, 68),
  valence = c(48, 65, 38, 42, 32, 22, 39, 58, 18, 69, 33, 73, 45),
  popularity = c(72, 68, 65, 74, 76, 84, 81, 66, 88, 89, 93, 75, 80)
)

# Load 5,000 background tracks from Spotify catalog
spotify_background <- read_csv("spotify_background.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Select a few recognizable reference tracks to label in the background
sample_labels <- spotify_background |>
  filter(title %in% c("Marvins Room", "Say So", "Hard Times", "Whole Lotta Love - 1990 Remaster", "One Less Lonely Girl")) |>
  mutate(clean_title = case_when(
    str_detect(title, "Whole Lotta Love") ~ "Whole Lotta Love (Led Zeppelin)",
    title == "Marvins Room" ~ "Marvins Room (Drake)",
    title == "Say So" ~ "Say So (Doja Cat)",
    title == "Hard Times" ~ "Hard Times (Paramore)",
    title == "One Less Lonely Girl" ~ "One Less Lonely Girl (Justin Bieber)",
    TRUE ~ title
  ))
```

## Sonic Profile Scatter Plot

Explore how my Top 5 songs compare to similar soul/bedroom pop tracks, dissimilar uptempo hits, and a broader sample of 5,000 Spotify tracks.

```{r}
#| label: spotify-scatter
#| fig-width: 9.5
#| fig-height: 6

ggplot() +
  # 1. Background cloud of 5,000 general Spotify songs
  geom_point(
    data = spotify_background,
    aes(x = tempo, y = energy),
    color = "grey85",
    alpha = 0.22,
    size = 0.8
  ) +
  # Subtle labels for a few recognizable background songs
  geom_text(
    data = sample_labels,
    aes(x = tempo, y = energy, label = clean_title),
    color = "grey35",
    size = 2.8,
    vjust = 1.4,
    check_overlap = TRUE
  ) +
  # 2. Foreground: Top 5 and comparison songs
  geom_point(
    data = songs_data,
    aes(x = tempo, y = energy, color = group, size = popularity),
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = songs_data,
    aes(x = tempo, y = energy, label = title),
    vjust = -1,
    size = 3.2,
    fontface = "bold",
    check_overlap = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(3, 8), name = "Popularity") +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Top 5" = "#1DB954",
      "Similar (Soul / Bedroom Pop)" = "#2E86AB",
      "Dissimilar (Uptempo / Dance / Trap)" = "#D64045"
    ),
    name = "Category"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(45, 190), breaks = seq(60, 180, by = 20)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(10, 95), breaks = seq(10, 90, by = 15)) +
  labs(
    title = "Why My Top 5 Songs Are My Top 5",
    subtitle = "Positioned against 5,000 Spotify catalog tracks (gray cloud) with recognizable landmarks labeled",
    x = "Tempo (Beats Per Minute)",
    y = "Energy Level (0–100)",
    caption = "Background: 5,000 tracks sampled from Spotify TidyTuesday catalog | Foreground: Personal profile"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```
